gen-gf-titillium-web-fs-literata: Titillium Web looks clean and contemporary, while Literata, a text serif, brings a faint shimmer of weight changes across each word. Titillium Web earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-tomorrow-fs-literata: Literata draws sturdy thin lines beside slightly heavier ones, while Tomorrow above it leaves spacious gaps at its curve ends. Page after page, the body stays comfortable and bookish.
gen-gf-trispace-fs-literata: Literata reads sturdy and bookish, with curves left unclosed at the mouth. What stands out is the spacing, with Trispace keeping letters well apart against Literata's medium-low stroke contrast.
gen-gf-trocchi-fs-bespoke-sans: Trocchi sounds authoritative and classic, its stroke weight shifting only gently. Bespoke Sans then reads sharp and refined, with generous space where curves meet the stem, so pages move along smoothly.
gen-gf-trykker-fs-bespoke-sans: Trykker feels literary and authoritative, its curvy, unclamped letters lightening slightly at joins and terminals. And where Trykker flows, Bespoke Sans stays sharp, leaving generous space between curve ends and the stem.
gen-gf-tsukimi-rounded-fs-literata: Technical-pen steadiness defines Tsukimi Rounded, a contemporary sans-serif with no pressure swells where the eye slows. Literata adds tempered contrast that never reaches razor-fine hairlines, keeping the text bookish and sturdy.
gen-gf-unna-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space between curve ends and stems, while Unna swings from hairline to heavy stroke. Give Bespoke Sans a little more size to show that off.
gen-gf-uoqmunthenkhung-fs-bespoke-sans: UoqMunThenKhung is authoritative and classic, pairing very fine thins with very thick thicks against Bespoke Sans, which stays low in contrast. Shrink the heading and those hairlines will fade.
gen-gf-urbanist-fs-literata: Clean Urbanist leads with open bowls and uniform strokes. Urbanist excels at flat strokes from stem to terminal, while Literata, a text serif, does better with its comfortable midpoint of contrast.
gen-gf-varela-round-fs-literata: Soft tubing-like strokes define Varela Round, with no hairlines anywhere, while Literata brings the restrained swell of a round brush. One is rounded and friendly, the other bookish and sturdy.
